- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward by 1–4% to reflect mean reversion.
- Model tends to lag in early days of a new trend (e.g., after sentiment shift); add 1–3 days of lagged sentiment to forecast adjustment.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts near-term volatility; cap forecast at 1.5x recent 7-day average to avoid extreme outliers.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model exhibits bias toward recent highs; use sentiment-weighted average of 3–5 prior days to anchor forecast.
